history.dynasty: Katoch dynasty of Kangra (Ambika is the clan goddess of the Katoch royal house); fort associated with the ancient Trigarta kingdom
history.period: Travel sources give 9th-11th century CE - CONFLICT / UNVERIFIED (verify); royal tradition calls it the oldest Ambika temple in India
history.summary: RELATED TO seq 373 (id "kangra-fort-temples", a composite entry for the fort's temple courtyard that lists Ambika Devi among several shrines); this file is the dedicated record for the Ambika Devi shrine itself. The temple stands inside Kangra Fort at Purana Kangra (Old Kangra). Ambika Devi is the kul devi (clan goddess) of the Katoch royal house: tradition says goddess Ambika created the dynasty's founder Bhumi Chandra from a drop of her perspiration during the Raktbeej battle (Markandeya Purana narrative), granted him the kingdom and the titles Rajanaka and Katoch, and is still worshipped by the royal family. The fort courtyard also holds the Laxmi Narayan, Shitala Mata, and Adinath Jain temples, a Shiva temple, Sheesh Mahal, and a mosque. One reviewer notes the shrine is under government supervision (verify). Coordinates given are for Kangra Fort (approximate; the temple stands within the fort complex).

name: Ambika Devi Temple, Kangra Fort
town_description: Old Kangra (Purana Kangra) is the historic settlement about 3 km from Kangra town, on a precipitous hill where the Manjhi and Ban Ganga rivers meet, where the ancient Kangra Fort stands. Once called Nagarkot, it was the capital of the Katoch kingdom and a strategic fortress that withstood many sieges from Mahmud of Ghazni onward. Today the fort and its temple courtyard are the area's main heritage attraction, reached from Kangra town by a short drive and a climb up many steps.

travel.airport: Kangra (Gaggal) airport, ~14 km from the fort (verify)
travel.railway: Kangra Mandi station (Pathankot-Jogindernagar narrow gauge), ~1.4 km from the fort
travel.road: Short drive from Kangra town to Old Kangra; the fort is reached through the Ranjit Singh Darwaza and requires climbing many steps to the temple courtyard
